title: Intelligent Applications Based on Medical Large Models to Enhance People's Healthcare Experience and Health Status
summary: Ant reports that its medical AI served 13 million users and improved annotation efficiency by 50%; individual health outcomes are not specified.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: Alipay describes medical assistants for residents, clinicians, and underserved areas. The submission reports 13 million users, 78 million service interactions, and a 50% improvement in the annotation workflow developed with medical specialists. Improved health and a more equitable distribution of care remain broader intended benefits.
purpose: Provide medical guidance and reduce administrative and information-processing work.
system: Ant medical large model and health-assistant agents
deployer: Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission; Hangzhou Municipal Medical Insurance Bureau; Renji Hospital

ratings.reason: The Ant/Renji development workflow reportedly improved annotation efficiency by 50%. Clinical outcomes are not reported.
The source reports broad uptake and 98% satisfaction, but does not quantify a change in health or individual service experience.
Healthcare equity and rural access are asserted aims without a measured distributional outcome.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 1: Intelligent Applications Based on Medical Large Models to Enhance People's Healthcare Experience and Health Status

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: Ant health assistants reach patients and support medical work
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
